01 / Type on your computer. Receive on your phone.

More to write?
Use the keyboard you know.

Reply to a message, take notes, or write a longer paragraph. Stay at your computer, compose with your usual keyboard and input method, then send it to your iPhone or iPad.

No extra software on your computer.

Switch to AirType on your phone, then open the keyboard’s address on your computer. On Mac, Windows, or Linux, a compatible browser is all you need.

02 / Keep typing on your phone

A few quick edits?
Make them on your phone.

AirType also includes a QWERTY keyboard. Switch back to local typing for a quick edit, or keep writing when you step away from your computer.

Web Access connects only while the keyboard is visible. Keep both devices on the same Wi-Fi and use a network you trust.

Get started with AirType

  1. Download and open AirType

    Download AirType from the App Store. If asked for Local Network access, choose Allow.

  2. Add the system keyboard

    Go to Settings → General → Keyboard → Keyboards → Add New Keyboard and choose AirType. Open its keyboard settings and enable Allow Full Access so it can use the network.

  3. Switch to AirType on your phone

    Open a normal text field, hold the globe key, and select AirType. Open Web Access and keep it visible.

  4. Open the connection address on your computer

    Your computer and phone must use the same Wi-Fi. Enter the keyboard’s complete address in your browser, including the port. If asked for a pairing code, enter the six digits shown on the keyboard.

  5. Type your message and press Enter

    Type your text and press Enter or click Send. It appears in the phone’s active text field. Press Shift + Enter to add a line break to your draft.

Addresses and connection steps may vary by app version. Follow what your keyboard shows. Some apps, secure password fields, and certain phone fields do not allow third-party keyboards.

FAQ

Do I need to install anything on my computer?

No. Open a compatible browser and enter the address shown on the AirType keyboard. Your computer and iPhone or iPad must be on the same Wi-Fi network.

Can I type Chinese and emoji?

Yes. Use your computer’s input method to compose Chinese, other languages, or emoji, then send the text to your phone. AirType’s local keyboard uses an English QWERTY and symbol layout.

Why does AirType need Full Access?

Third-party iOS keyboards need Full Access to use networking. If iOS also asks for Local Network access, allow it too. Use AirType only on Wi-Fi networks you trust.

What if the page won’t open or the connection drops?

Keep Web Access visible, check that both devices use the same Wi-Fi, and verify the address and port. If the .local address fails, try the IP address shown on the keyboard. Guest Wi-Fi, client isolation, or a VPN may block the connection. If the page shows Reconnect, reopen the keyboard and click it.

Does this website’s demo send my text anywhere?

No. The demo runs only in this page and resets when you refresh. To send text to your phone, download AirType and open the local address shown on its keyboard.

Privacy and connections

This website’s interactive demo

Demo text is processed only in this page. It is not sent to an AirType device or server and is not kept after a refresh. This page does not include analytics, advertising trackers, or cookies.

Using AirType

Web Access sends text over your local network to the active text field on your phone. Use trusted Wi-Fi. Local HTTP connections are unencrypted; do not send sensitive content over public or untrusted networks.
